executiveSummary: GM1954 passes the complete deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, headline demography, 29 neighbourhoods, fourteen BAG places, fifty BRT settlements, eleven NWB links, two stations, null semantics, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, exact zero-intensity behavior and sustained-water repair guard are coherent. Release remains correction-required for two related spatial-evidence failures. The named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset assigns Beekdaelen sustained direct municipality-wide inundation stress from a coarse line-distance field without selecting a connected Maas/tributary scenario: internal stress reaches 1.371341 at T+12, remains through T+72 and yields 15,296 modeled people under pressure and 1,209,494 cumulative event-attributable service person-hours at T+72. Official regional and local evidence instead distinguishes the Maas from Geul, Gulp, Geleenbeek and local steep-slope runoff, while Waterschap Limburg identifies specific pathways and T25/T100 studies at Hegge, Wijnandsrade, Aalbeek and Hulsberg. All water mechanisms nevertheless inherit one deterministic neighbourhood ordering: Amstenrade ranks first for river, coastal and pluvial, while Wijnandsrade and Nagelbeek-Hegge rank sixteenth and eighteenth for pluvial. The public layer usefully exposes 105 official-context water objects, and public provider lookup identifies Enexis, but neither changes simulation. All eight utility views honestly call their shared A76/A79/N-road/Laar flows logical transfer proxies. Physical WML, Enexis, sewer, telecom, facility and emergency-supply topology, live state, backup, stock, crews and restoration estimates remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 — filtered municipality row GM1954
supports: Official-context GM1954/Beekdaelen identity, population 35,824 and density 458 residents per square kilometre.
Official age-65-plus count 10,064, equivalent to the generated rounded share 28.1%, and 5,336 one-person households.
The OData table is machine-readable, updated annually and published under CC BY 4.0; rounded/suppressed neighbourhood values require explicit null and reconciliation semantics.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek
evidenceSources.title: Gemeente gegeneraliseerd 2025
supports: Official annual CC BY 4.0 generalized GM1954 polygon consumed by the application.
Municipality-centre point-in-polygon validation and the administrative polygon used for neighbourhood and public-asset intersections.
The generalized CBS boundary is not a drainage catchment, flow path, flood extent, forest perimeter, provider territory or cross-border transport service area.

evidenceSources.title: Provinciaal Risicoprofiel Limburg 2023–2027
supports: Official strategic scenario/context evidence distinguishes the Maas and tributaries including Geul, Gulp and Geleenbeek and identifies South Limburg's hills, vulnerable soil and cross-border setting.

The all-hazard list includes river flooding, dike failure, nature fire, storm, drought, earthquake, cold, heat, extreme rain, cyberattack, and loss of gas, electricity, drinking water, wastewater treatment and communications.

The profile identifies A76, A79, N276, N281 and N300 as important regional roads and says South Limburg's narrow connection to the rest of the Netherlands makes cross-border cooperation important for crisis response.

WML, Waterschapsbedrijf Limburg, Waterschap Limburg, Enexis, TenneT, Gasunie, ProRail, KNMI, RIVM and a telecom representative contributed, supporting dependency relevance but not any exact GM1954 topology, capacity or restoration value.
This is an official four-year strategic risk product, not a live/observed feed or machine-readable municipality footprint; no dataset redistribution licence is stated in the publication.

evidenceSources.title: Aanpak wateroverlast Hegge Schinnen
supports: Official local historical/context evidence reports repeated water nuisance around Hegge and severe damage during the extreme May 2018 downpours, including runoff and mud from recently ploughed rural slopes.
The local mechanism explicitly spans hills/rural land, the built area around Hegge, the Hegge buffer and property-level resilience rather than a municipality-wide scalar.
The page identifies a new Hegge rain buffer, optimisation of Diependaalsweg and Heggerweg buffers and directed flow paths as local measures.

This current project page is authoritative local context, not a machine-readable runoff/depth surface, live buffer state or licensed operations feed; no fixed update cadence or reuse licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Aanpak wateroverlast Wijnandsrade, Aalbeek en Hulsberg
supports: Official local evidence reports recurring water nuisance around Wijnandsrade castle despite six buffers, runoff from southern rural land toward Aalbeek/N298, and road flow toward Wissengracht and Hulsbergerbeek in Hulsberg.
The authority assessed streams, slopes, overland flow and surroundings and publishes location-specific T25/T100 map images for Hulsberg; the project sits in the Hekerbeek/Geul catchment programme.

The T25/T100 downloads are scenario/context images, not observed/live state and not a documented machine GIS endpoint. The current project page is updated irregularly with project milestones; no explicit redistribution licence for the map images/native model was found.

evidenceSources.title: Nieuwe elektriciteitshuisjes in Beekdaelen
supports: Official local context identifies Enexis as the distribution operator and describes planned reinforcement across many villages with at least 200 additional transformer cabinets plus underground cables; final sites/counts were not yet known.

Enexis publishes machine-readable electricity/gas Asset Data CSV ZIPs at https://data.overheid.nl/dataset/enexis-assetdata under CC0 1.0; the catalogue metadata was last updated 2023-01-31 and declares no periodic refresh cadence.
Public asset records can support provider-specific static context but not current switching, capacity, load, failure, backup, crew or restoration claims.

evidenceSources.title: Nationaal Wegenbestand Wegen OGC API
supports: Machine-readable road-section geometry underlying GM1954's eleven A76/A79/N300/N298/N274/N276/Laar cross-boundary logical routes.
NWB is continuously maintained and normally released monthly under CC0; the current OGC landing exposes the licence but no updateFrequency field, so snapshot edition remains essential.
NWB represents static road geometry and identity, not current closure, congestion, bridge/tunnel state, emergency access, evacuation throughput or utility capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO OGC APIs
supports: Machine-readable object-level official context; the current generalized-boundary intersection contains 105 objects: 97 weirs, three surface-water pumps and five sewer pumps.
Named examples include Rioolgemaal Nuth, Schinnen, Schimmert and Vaesrade, the emergency pump at Burgemeester Pijlsstraat, Gemaal Kakkert and multiple buffer overflows.

Kunstwerken IMWA and companion Waterketen DAMO at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are CC BY-SA 4.0. The current landing metadata exposes no fixed updateFrequency and contributor completeness varies, so object timestamps and retrieval time must be retained.

The collection is explicitly official-context, partial and affectsSimulation=false; object presence/status does not prove hydraulic connectivity, controls, capacity, emergency power, live availability or restoration time.

notes: The generated feature id, municipality bundle code and name equal GM1954/Beekdaelen.
The safety-region layer assigns GM1954 to exactly one region, Limburg-Zuid; the provincial profile covers both Limburg regions and their shared hazards.
No identity, province or safety-region mismatch was found.

geography.summary: The consumed 2025 generalized municipality polygon and centre are coherent, while catchments, flow paths and cross-border systems retain distinct semantics.
notes: Generated centre [5.891135798449782, 50.95358629087244] is inside the official generalized GM1954 polygon.
BoundaryEdition and statisticsEdition both equal 2025.

CBS municipality/neighbourhoods, BAG woonplaatsen, BRT settlements, water catchments and provider areas are not collapsed into one geography.

demography.summary: Headline municipality statistics match CBS 2025 and rounded neighbourhood population reconciles within publication precision.
notes: Generated population 35,824, density 458 and one-person-household count 5,336 exactly match the filtered CBS municipality row.
Generated age65Pct 28.1 is the rounded share implied by the official 10,064 residents aged 65 or older.
The 29 published neighbourhoods sum to 35,810 residents, fourteen below the municipality row (-0.039%); households sum to 16,435 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 10,070.
The small reconciliation differences are disclosed as independent CBS rounding rather than silently treated as missing residents.

regionalDetail.summary: All 29 neighbourhoods expose broad aggregate context, but suppressions remain null and these fields do not locate individual need or physical hazard.
notes: Address density, all age bands, household variables, businesses, cars, homes, land/water, GP/supermarket distance, urbanity and population density are available in all 29 neighbourhoods.
Home value, housing form and tenure percentages are available in 27/29; cars per household in 26/29 and benefit-recipient indicators in 28/29.
District-heating percentage and public-charging-point count are unavailable in all 29 and correctly remain null rather than zero.

The municipality's 28.1% older-resident share and rural distance/car variables are useful aggregate allocation context, not individual dependency, vehicle availability, household preparedness or evacuation observation.
Compound T+24 local population, affected people and all service demand/delivery totals reconcile exactly to the municipality frame.

settlements.summary: Fourteen BAG woonplaatsen and fifty BRT settlements remain distinct from CBS administration and neighbourhood population.
notes: The fourteen active BAG places are Amstenrade, Bingelrade, Doenrade, Hulsberg, Jabeek, Merkelbeek, Nuth, Oirsbeek, Puth, Schimmert, Schinnen, Schinveld, Sweikhuizen and Wijnandsrade; all label centres are inside the generalized boundary.
BRT contributes fifty settlements: six buurtschappen, twenty deelkernen, three gehuchten and twenty-one woonkernen.
Neither the fourteen BAG units nor the denser BRT label set is substituted for official GM1954 population or the 29 CBS neighbourhoods.

transport.summary: Eleven NWB routes, two stations and scheduled stops are structurally valid, but they omit foreign response nodes and use generalized logical capacity.
notes: Routes connect six Dutch municipalities—Heerlen, Voerendaal, Brunssum, Valkenburg aan de Geul, Beek and Sittard-Geleen—through A76, A79, N300, N298, N274, N276 and Laar sections; all endpoints resolve.

Four motorway routes use logical capacity 260 and seven other sections 150, totaling 2,090 scenario units in every service view. The 0.1 km Laar crossing is a source-labelled road section, not evidence of N-road-equivalent emergency throughput.
Nuth and Schinnen stations and sixty GTFS stop areas are present as static context.
No German municipality, emergency-assistance gateway or cross-border road/rail operating state is represented despite E03's Euregional response dependency.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative sources establish steep-slope runoff, named buffers/streams, cross-border dependencies and local grid reinforcement that the generic model does not causally encode.
notes: E04/E05 locate real runoff routes and measures in Hegge, Wijnandsrade, Aalbeek and Hulsberg rather than a uniform municipal exposure.
E03 provides an all-hazard regional dependency catalogue and identifies cross-border cooperation, but not local event probabilities, inventories or response capacities.
E06 identifies Enexis and at least 200 planned transformer cabinets while explicitly saying final locations/counts were not yet known.

The map's current public provider lookup correctly resolves Enexis at the municipality reference point, and 105 water objects plus four coarse government-service points remain non-causal official context.
No sensitive/operational topology, live state, facility role/capacity, backup, stock, crew or restoration commitment was inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at all six required checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Peak municipality severities were storm 0.495666, pluvial 0.291646, river 0.434246, coastal 0.012826, heat 0.434260, winter 0.521362, cyber 0.538022, earthquake 0.001951, wildfire 0.127353 and compound 0.814288.

At T+24 compound had rain 40.571624 mm/h, inundation-stress amplitude 0.215608, wind 24.746448 m/s, cyber disruption 0.472005, system pressure 0.507998, 18,574 modeled people under pressure and 329,666 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours.

At T+72 compound retained inundation-stress amplitude 0.215596 and cyber disruption 0.061389, with severity 0.262469, pressure 0.545261, 20,454 people under pressure and 1,237,755 cumulative proxy person-hours.
apps/web/src/scenarios.ts clones canonical sim-core presets. All numbers are deterministic derived scenario estimates, not observed local weather, probability, incident or outage data.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, monotonic cumulative burden, route bounds and local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1954 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 26.60 seconds.
Every canonical preset at intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated frames are deterministic; state is finite/bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; and route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciles municipality population 35,824, affected population 18,574 and all eight demand/delivery balances, with maximum floating-point discrepancy 3.56e-15.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The generic major-river field and shared seeded neighbourhood ranking do not represent Beekdaelen's Maas/tributary distinction, hills, streams, buffers or mapped runoff paths.
notes: River stress rises from zero at T+0 to 0.482712 at T+6 and 1.371341 at T+12, remaining 1.371341 through T+72; affected population is 17,311 at T+12, 13,663 at T+24 and 15,296 at T+48/T+72.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-458 derives river exposure from the municipality centre's distance to three coarse diagonal segments; lines 603-608 apply a scalar without a named Maas/tributary event, connected footprint, water level, defence, depth, arrival or duration layer.
E03 distinguishes Maas and tributaries, while E04/E05 identify slope-to-street/buffer/stream paths at Hegge, Wijnandsrade, Aalbeek and Hulsberg; none causes the generic municipality-wide result.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3337 onward applies municipality severity × a deterministic regional seed. River, coastal and pluvial therefore have the identical exact ranking across all 29 neighbourhoods.

At pluvial T+24 Amstenrade ranks first at 0.176368; documented Aalbeek ranks third at 0.171462, Hulsberg eighth at 0.165867, Wijnandsrade sixteenth at 0.156190 and Nagelbeek-Hegge eighteenth at 0.154002. The deterministic order is not the T25/T100/runoff evidence offered by E04/E05.
Coastal direct inundation remains exactly zero, correctly separating inland direct water from its preset's small wind-only indirect stress.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances and dependencies are inspectable, but their magnitudes are not calibrated to Beekdaelen assets, providers or cross-border response.
notes: River T+24 availability was power 0.390407, water 0.755225, drainage 0.352715, gas 0.841740, telecom 0.741015, mobility 0.681905, facilities 0.784751 and supply 0.176211.
Compound T+24 availability was power 0.196271, water 0.629744, drainage 0.222400, gas 0.761299, telecom 0.432826, mobility 0.263905, facilities 0.761958 and supply 0.713508.
E03 supports direction of vital-process dependencies, but no source calibrates those exact availability, demand, delivery or repair values.

The causal graph has no named Hegge/Wijnandsrade catchment or buffer, public sewer-pump node, WML pressure zone, Enexis station, telecom site, emergency facility role, stock depot or German assistance node.
All eight service views reuse the same eleven NWB-derived routes and nominal total 2,090; emitted transferSemantics is consistently logical-proxy.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve scenario confidence, controls, dependency ordering and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, drivers, local vulnerability/demand factors, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness changes modeled people/supply consequences after physical pressure rather than changing physical hazard fragility.
Operational controls and time-gated interventions are labeled scenario assumptions; shared road-derived utility flows remain logical proxies.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure against a matched no-event baseline and are not observed customer outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water and response-delay safeguards behave consistently, but unsupported spatial forcing and absent resources prevent operational recovery interpretation.
notes: River forcing remains active at T+72, all eight service recovery-progress values remain exactly zero, pressure is 0.443065, 15,296 people remain under pressure and cumulative proxy burden reaches 1,209,494 person-hours.
River T+72 keeps seven service availabilities at their T+24 values while facilities declines from 0.784751 to 0.553629 through generic dependencies; this is not a local care/operator forecast.
Pluvial water clears by T+48 and T+72 pressure falls to 0.073313 with no affected population; recovery progress reaches 0.962475–1. Compound retains 0.215596 generic water and zero recovery at T+72.
Ended storm, winter, wildfire and earthquake forcing recovers monotonically; the two-week heatwave and cyber schedule retain bounded forcing through T+72.
Actual runoff clearance, buffers, wastewater controls, provider switching, roads, foreign assistance, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, staffing, stock and restoration estimates are unknown.

findings.summary: A coarse proximity corridor creates unsupported sustained direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation across Beekdaelen.
findings.evidence: E03 distinguishes the Maas from the Geul, Gulp and Geleenbeek; E04/E05 establish local hill-runoff, buffer, Hekerbeek/Geul and Hulsbergerbeek pathways. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-458 instead measures the GM1954 centroid against three coarse diagonal segments and lines 603-608 turn that screen into direct water. The canonical named-major-river frame emits internal inundation stress 0.482712 at T+6 and 1.371341 at T+12 through T+72, with 13,663 modeled people and 303,543 event-attributable service person-hours at T+24 and 15,296 people/1,209,494 person-hours at T+72. All restoration remains zero because the synthetic water persists. The UI exposes 91% normalized inundation stress and 15.3K under pressure at T+72 with spatialEvidence derived-screening rather than Unknown. No selected connected scenario, defence, water level, depth, arrival or duration supports that exact municipality-wide result. This is municipality-specific evidence of the shared national proximity-field defect, not a claim that Beekdaelen lacks river/stream flood risk.
findings.action: Mark GM1954's current direct named-major-river result unsupported/Unknown and numerically neutral in downstream decisions until an expert-selected source footprint exists; preserve local tributary/runoff risk as unresolved rather than safe. The durable fix must intersect a named/versioned LIWO or water-board scenario, separately model Maas, Geul/Hekerbeek/Geleenbeek and overland-flow mechanisms, and expose affected population only inside a connected approved footprint.

findings.summary: One seeded neighbourhood order replaces Beekdaelen's documented mechanism-specific slopes, streams, roads and buffers.
findings.evidence: E04/E05 provide named local mechanisms and T25/T100 map images: slope/mud flow into Hegge, runoff toward Aalbeek/N298, repeated Wijnandsrade castle-area nuisance and road flow to Wissengracht/Hulsbergerbeek. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3337 onward uses one deterministic hazardSeed multiplier for local severity. Exact rankings are identical across river, coastal and pluvial: Amstenrade first, while Wijnandsrade is 16/29 and Nagelbeek-Hegge 18/29 in pluvial at T+24. Pluvial municipality stress 0.208033, 9,637 modeled people and pressure 0.330943 at T+24 are reproducible, but no official runoff cell, terrain, stream, street, buffer or asset drives their allocation. The shared hash also cannot make coastal, main-river and convective-runoff footprints physically different.
findings.action: Mark neighbourhood direct-water distribution unsupported until a versioned source layer is supplied. Obtain the native GIS/model output behind E05's T25/T100 images and E04's Hegge project, intersect it with 2025 neighbourhood geometry and preserve resolution, units, return period, edition, no-data and uncertainty. Use AHN/IMWA/GWSW as disclosed covariates only, and add fixtures proving mechanism-specific ranks and source-footprint containment.

findings.summary: Named buffers, sewer pumps and overland flow paths remain non-causal in drainage and mobility response.
findings.evidence: E04/E05 name implemented/planned buffers and directed flows; E08 exposes 105 official objects, including five named sewer pumps, three surface-water pumps and 97 weirs/overflows. The application correctly marks these assets official-context, partial and affectsSimulation=false. Pluvial T+24 drainage/mobility service values and T+48 recovery therefore result from generic hazard, network and repair equations, not Hegge buffer operation, Hulsbergerbeek capacity, N298 passability, emergency pumping, sewer connectivity, backup power or monitored state.
findings.action: Retain public assets as non-causal context until Waterschap Limburg/municipality provide licensed topology, controls, capacity and state suitable for exercises. Add catchment-to-road/service dependencies only with approved evidence; otherwise use a bounded service-specific scenario fallback that names the assumed buffer/pump state and never infers performance from a point feature.

findings.summary: The first-72-hour graph omits Beekdaelen's German-border assistance and access context.
findings.evidence: E02 places the eastern municipality boundary on the national frontier, and E03 says South Limburg's narrow Dutch connection makes neighbouring-country cooperation important for crisis response. The generated graph contains eleven routes to six Dutch municipalities only; no German external node, cross-border road/rail gateway, mutual-aid travel time or border disruption state exists. This omission is especially relevant to mobility, facilities and emergency supply, while it must not be cloned into power/water/gas topology.
findings.action: Add an explicitly external, mobility/facilities/supply-only exercise gateway after validating a cross-border route and response agreement. Use NWB/NDW to the Dutch frontier and an authoritative German/European road source with its licence/edition where obtainable; if operational agreements/capacity are unavailable, keep generalized scenario capacity, delay and availability editable and label them synthetic.

findings.summary: Provider responsibility is correctly identified, but physical Enexis/WML/telecom topology and operational state are absent.
findings.evidence: E06 and the live public provider-territory lookup identify Enexis at the municipality reference point. The UI correctly says the provider polygon is responsibility context only and that Liander geometry is visible only in Liander territory; an empty local Liander result is not presented as no asset. E06's public CC0 Enexis downloads can add static context, but their catalogue metadata was last updated in 2023 and gives no periodic cadence. No adequate safe public WML pressure-zone, telecom access/backhaul or live provider-state feed was established.
findings.action: Ingest Enexis CC0 electricity/gas files as provider-specific affectsSimulation=false context with file date, coverage and catalogue-staleness warning. Keep WML/telecom physical topology, capacity, switching, pressure, outage, backup, crews and restoration unknown unless an operator supplies an authorized exercise dataset; use only the smallest visibly synthetic service-specific fallback.

findings.summary: All eight essential services reuse eleven road crossings and generalized capacity rather than service-specific topology.
findings.evidence: Each service repeats A76 ×2, A79 ×2, N300 ×2, N298, N274, N276 ×2 and the 0.1 km Laar section, with the same nominal sum 2,090. E07 supports road identity/geometry only; E03 supports dependency relevance but not cable, pipe, pressure-zone, telecom, care or food topology. Every emitted edge correctly declares transferSemantics logical-proxy, and the UI fidelity badge states ‘logical service transfers’, avoiding a direct physical-network claim.
findings.action: Keep the fidelity warning and separate public context from causal flows. Promote an edge to physical only with provider-approved topology, direction, capacity, backup and current state. Until then retain distinct service-specific logical graphs and do not imply that NWB class or a 100 m boundary section measures utility or emergency throughput.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter and cyber outputs are scenario stressors rather than dated Beekdaelen observations, warnings or incidents.
findings.evidence: E03 establishes regional relevance for storm, heat, drought, cold, extreme rain, cyber and vital-service interruption. Model peaks—storm 0.495666, heat 0.434260, winter 0.521362 and cyber 0.538022—come from canonical schedules and deterministic seeds. At T+72 heat retains drought/current severity 0.395644/0.071216 and cyber disruption 0.053802; no KNMI grid/station timestamp, warning validity, measured local heat exposure, named cyber target, provider incident or outage observation supports the exact values.
findings.action: Keep scenario/evidence confidence prominent. Optionally ingest KNMI Open Data/Data Platform observations, grids and warnings with product resolution, issue/valid time, update interval and licence, and accept only authorized cyber targets/state; never label a preset as forecast, probability or current outage.

findings.summary: Coastal, remote Groningen-earthquake and remote-wildfire cases are bounded but do not replace locally selected Limburg hazards.
findings.evidence: Coastal direct water is exactly zero at every checkpoint; T+24 wind 20.940594 m/s produces low severity 0.012826 and 793 people under pressure before affected population returns to zero at T+72. The remote Groningen earthquake peaks at 0.001951, has zero current shaking/affected population at T+24 and accumulates 1,650 proxy person-hours by T+72. Remote wildfire has zero direct flame, smoke 0.210633 and drought 0.710217 at T+24, with zero affected population. E03 separately lists Limburg earthquake and nature-fire risk; these presets have no local event, ground-motion, fault/mine, fuel, perimeter, wind-spread or suppression evidence.
findings.action: Retain remote-event names and direct/indirect separation. Use the automatically updated KNMI earthquake catalogue at https://www.knmi.nl/kennis-en-datacentrum/dataset/aardbevingscatalogus (JSON/CSV/KML updated when an event is published; licence not stated on that page) plus event-specific ground motion and fragility for a local event. Use BRT TOP10NL terrain polygons (1:10,000, CC BY 4.0, normally annual) and explicit incident/weather inputs for local fire; land cover alone is not fuel condition or spread.

findings.summary: Official identity, rounded demography, null handling, settlement products and local service allocation are inspectably coherent.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 agree with GM1954 identity and headline totals. All 29 neighbourhoods retain unavailable values as null; their rounded population is only fourteen below the municipality row; all fourteen BAG place centres are inside; BAG/BRT/CBS semantics stay separate; and compound T+24 local population, affected people, demand and delivery reconcile municipality values for all eight services. Aggregate vulnerability/activity inputs influence service-specific allocation without claiming individual need or measured load.
findings.action: Retain source editions, null semantics, distinct geographic products, aggregate-context disclosure and exact municipality/local reconciliation tests.

findings.summary: The deterministic, causal, no-event, layer-invariance and sustained-water contracts pass for GM1954.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passed ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services; intensity zero exactly clears event severity/peak/affected/person-hours; repeated frames are deterministic; numerical and route bounds hold; all explanation/counterfactual ledgers close; map-layer selection cannot change physical state; and sustained water blocks elapsed-time repair. The current UI exposes all eleven layers, normalized inundation stress, scenario evidence labels, public Enexis responsibility context, partial non-causal water context and logical-service-transfer fidelity rather than metres or physical utility topology.
findings.action: Preserve these national invariants while correcting GM1954-RIVER-001 and GM1954-WATER-SPAT-001; add exact unsupported-evidence and selected-footprint fixtures without weakening zero-intensity or reconciliation behavior.

corrections.summary: Stop exposing Beekdaelen's generic named-major-river proximity value as a supported local inundation result and require a selected connected scenario.
corrections.validation: Interim: retain the current scalar only as a diagnostic, set GM1954 river spatialEvidence to unsupported, expose the direct local result as Unknown and make unsupported direct forcing numerically neutral downstream; state that Geul/Hekerbeek/Geleenbeek and local runoff remain unresolved rather than safe. Re-run pnpm test plus focused and ALL municipality gates. Durable machine source: LIWO GeoServer OWS https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows and catalogue API https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 expose named/versioned scenario rasters for depth, arrival and duration. LIWO is release/layer-versioned rather than fixed-cadence and its public portal does not expose one blanket redistribution licence; store layer/scenario/version/retrieval and clear terms before caching. Waterschapshuis Oppervlaktewateren IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-oppervlaktewateren-imwa/ogc/v1 and Keringen IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-keringen-imwa/ogc/v1 are national machine vectors under CC0 with no fixed cadence on the current landing; use object timestamps/coverage to distinguish waterways/defences but never infer inundation from line presence alone.

corrections.summary: Replace seeded Beekdaelen water allocation with source-specific terrain, catchment, runoff and buffer evidence.
corrections.validation: Request the native GIS/model grids behind E05's published T25/T100 Hulsberg images and E04's Hegge project; record publisher, model/return period, cell resolution, units, edition, temporal validity, no-data, uncertainty and reuse terms. The project pages update with milestones but expose no stable API or reuse licence, so do not digitize the JPG/PDF presentation layers. Integration-ready public covariates are AHN WCS https://service.pdok.nl/rws/actueel-hoogtebestand-nederland/wcs/v1_0?SERVICE=WCS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities (Rijkswaterstaat/PDOK DTM/DSM, 0.5 m products, cyclical AHN editions, CC0), GWSW OGC https://api.pdok.nl/rioned/waterschappen-waterketen-gwsw/ogc/v1 (sewer context, CC0, current landing cadence unspecified), and E08 IMWA/DAMO objects (object-level, CC BY-SA 4.0, variable completeness/cadence). Tests must make approved runoff cells—not a hash—govern direct local water, permit river/coastal/pluvial orderings to differ, and never describe elevation, a stream line or point asset as calibrated depth/capacity.

corrections.summary: Add provider-specific and cross-border planning context without inventing operational topology or emergency capacity.
corrections.validation: Ingest Enexis Asset Data electricity/gas CSV ZIPs from https://data.overheid.nl/dataset/enexis-assetdata as provider-specific official-context only: CC0 1.0, object/segment records, catalogue metadata last updated 2023-01-31, no declared recurring cadence, large files and unknown operational freshness. Keep the existing live Stichting Mijn Aansluiting WMS/WFS provider territory (Public Domain; provider-supplied updates with varying timestamps) and E08 assets affectsSimulation=false. Retain NWB road geometry (monthly release, CC0), and optionally add timestamped NDW DATEX II feeds from https://opendata.ndw.nu/ for Dutch speed/intensity/incidents/closures with each feed's licence/validity. A German/external assistance gateway may affect only mobility, facilities and supply after authoritative route/agreement review; absent capacity should remain an editable delayed synthetic scenario. No safe public operational WML pressure/topology, Enexis switching/state, telecom topology, care capacity or first-72-hour food/fuel inventory was found; do not infer these from provider polygons or static assets.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved Beekdaelen LIWO/water-board depth, arrival, duration, defence, tributary, runoff or catchment grid is ingested; normalized inundation stress is not measured metres.
Marking unsupported Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing Unknown must not erase actual Geul/Hekerbeek/Geleenbeek, Hulsbergerbeek, slope-runoff, mudflow, groundwater, sewer-overload or buffer mechanisms.
Waterschap and municipality project pages are authoritative local context and publish some T25/T100 images, but not a licensed native machine model, live buffer state or operational forecast.

CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve buildings, terrain depressions, slopes, cellars, streams, culverts, buffers, sewers, pumps, households, workers, visitors or individual vulnerability.

The public Waterschapshuis layer is intentionally partial; its 105 intersecting points cannot be interpreted as a complete municipal/water-board system or reconciled to differently scoped infrastructure inventories.
The current provider polygon correctly names Enexis but is not network geometry; Enexis public Asset Data catalogue metadata is old and does not establish current operation.
No physical WML, Enexis, wastewater, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, current state, backup, priority-customer list, crew, fuel, spare or restoration estimate is available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
The national-only graph omits German access, agencies, hospitals, suppliers and mutual aid; no operational cross-border agreement or capacity was inferred.
Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS inputs do not establish live closure, timetable/vehicle operation, bridge/tunnel state, congestion, evacuation throughput or repair access.
Facilities and supply lack verified care roles, beds, staff, acceptance, care-home occupancy, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
The regional profile includes hazardous-material, aviation and other crisis types—including nearby cross-border context—not represented by the ten canonical presets.

Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, fuel/moisture condition, wind-aware spread, smoke dispersion, access and suppression state; earthquake lacks a selected Limburg event, ground motion, site response and asset fragility.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Beekdaelen resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, slope-flow peaks, dispatch and restrictions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
provinceReviewFlags: Review every Limburg municipality receiving direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel stress from the shared line-distance function against a selected connected LIWO scenario; distinguish Maas main-river flooding from Geul, Gulp, Geleenbeek and local stream/runoff mechanisms.

Replace shared neighbourhood water seeds across South Limburg with licensed T25/T100/runoff products, AHN terrain and water-board catchment/assets while preserving return period, resolution, no-data, version and licence.
Audit hilly-landscape runoff, mudflow, road/tunnel access and buffer clearance separately from flat-area pluvial assumptions and municipality density.
Coordinate Enexis, WML, Waterschapsbedrijf Limburg, Waterschap Limburg, provider territories and public facilities as non-causal context unless authorized operational topology/state is supplied.

Review Dutch-only graphs for every German/Belgian border municipality; introduce service-eligible external gateways only with authoritative route/agreement evidence and visibly generalized scenario capacity.
